article.headline: Zscaler Slips 1.6% As Cybersecurity Stocks Swing With AI Trade
article.deck: Zscaler sits at the top of its 191.35 to 200.92 buy range from a 15-week deep cup, but it has dropped below its 50-day line.
body: Zscaler fell 3.33 to 200.55, down 1.6%, as of 12:58 p.m. Mountain. The stock broke out of a 15-week deep cup, 37.5% deep, on Sept. 14 and has spent the 39 sessions since inside the buy range, which runs from the 191.35 buy point to 200.92. Today's price is 4.8% above the buy point, right at the top of the range. Volume is on pace for 0.63x its 50-day average.

The base formed after a bigger correction: Zscaler is still well below its 336.99 high from Nov. 3, 2025, and the 52-week high of 333.90 is 39.9% overhead. The stock slipped under its 50-day line at 208.07 and now trades 3.6% below it. The 21-day line at 224.34 is further up, and the stock is 1.06 ATRs under it. The 200-day line at 167.01 sits 20.1% below. The RS line is 44.0% below its high, and Zscaler holds RS rank 62 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are down 10.8% this year and 38.1% over twelve months.

In the July quarter Zscaler lost 0.02 a share on revenue of $898.2 million, up 24.9% from a year earlier. Its quarterly losses have narrowed from 0.21 a share in the January quarter to 0.09 and then 0.02. The next report is due Dec. 2. Market value is about $32.7 billion at 35.7 times forward earnings.

The group has been whipsawing. TIKR reported Thursday that CrowdStrike sank 9%, Palo Alto 8% and Cloudflare 9% as the AI trade unwound, and Friday that CrowdStrike and Palo Alto each rebounded 2%. Zacks noted Zscaler dipped more than the broader market Thursday.
article.watch: Whether Zscaler can get back above its 50-day line at 208.07 or slips under the 191.35 buy point.

article.headline: Grainger Holds Near Highs After Earnings Beat And Double-Digit Sales Growth
article.deck: Grainger is in the buy range two sessions after breaking out of a 15-week flat base, 1.8% above its 1420.01 buy point with the range running to 1491.01.
body: W.W. Grainger slipped 5.47 to 1445.92, down 0.4%, as of 12:58 p.m. Mountain, two sessions after it broke out of a 15-week flat base. The base was 12.9% deep, and the buy point is 1420.01. The stock is 1.8% above it, inside the buy range that tops out at 1491.01. Breakout day on Nov. 4 traded 2.39x the 50-day average. Today is on pace for 0.52x.

The 52-week high of 1521.41 is 5.0% above. Grainger sits 10.2% over its 50-day line at 1312.24 and 1.63 ATRs above its 21-day line at 1369.74, so the trend is intact without being stretched. The RS line is 1.0% below its high, and the stock holds RS rank 91 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 43.3% this year and 50.2% over twelve months.

September-quarter earnings came to 12.42 a share, up 102.9% from a year earlier, on revenue of $5.18 billion, up 11.3%. Quarterly earnings have climbed from 9.44 a share in the December quarter to 11.65, 12.01 and now 12.42. The next report is expected Feb. 2. Grainger is valued at about $67.7 billion and trades at 28.3 times forward earnings.

The breakout came with the third-quarter report. GuruFocus headlined the earnings call highlights as double-digit sales growth, and Simply Wall St. ran a piece Friday calling the earnings beat a possible game changer for the stock.
A close back under 1420.01 would turn the breakout into a stall.
article.watch: Whether Grainger holds above the 1420.01 buy point while it trades in the range up to 1491.01.

article.headline: Natera Tumbles 14.7% On Wider Third-Quarter Loss And Sudden CEO Change
article.deck: The drop knocked Natera 29.1% below the 437.51 buy point of a five-week cup and under its 50-day line, so it is nowhere near a buy point.
body: Natera dropped 53.56 to 310.20, down 14.7%, as of 12:58 p.m. Mountain. Volume is on pace for 2.82x its 50-day average. The stock had been building a five-week cup off a rim dated Oct. 6, and the buy point is 437.51. Today's slide cut the base to 30.5% deep with an intraday low of 304.00, and the stock now sits 29.1% below the buy point.

Natera broke through its 50-day line at 380.24 and now trades 18.4% under it. It is 2.58 ATRs below the 21-day line at 389.06. The 200-day line at 269.35 is still 15.2% below. The RS line is 25.8% off its high, and the stock holds RS rank 86 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares remain up 35.4% this year and 55.2% over twelve months, and the 52-week high of 437.41 is 29.1% overhead.

The quarters table runs only through June, when Natera lost 0.47 a share on revenue of $752.8 million, up 37.7% from a year earlier. Revenue has risen each quarter shown, from $592.2 million in the September 2025 quarter. Natera is valued at about $44.7 billion.

The company reported third-quarter results Thursday. MT Newswires reported the shares fell after a wider-than-expected loss, and MedTech Dive reported Natera promoted Solomon Moshkevich to CEO. GuruFocus tied the slide to the wider loss and the sudden CEO change. RBC said the results and a 2029 revenue target support the growth outlook, per MT Newswires.
The chart needs a new base and a recovery of the 50-day line before a buy point means anything.
article.watch: Whether Natera holds today's 304.00 low in the sessions ahead.
